citations.F1: `serialize_event` runs one `users` query per event, sequentially awaited, so ~1,000 round trips per request; fetch all actors once with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: Dedupe uses a `list` for `seen`, so membership is O(n²); move dedupe into SQL (`DISTINCT ON (dedupe_key)`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses blocking `requests.get` inside an async handler, so every cache miss ... freezes the worker's event loop and `/healthz` with it; switch to `httpx.AsyncClient`
citations.F4: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`; there is no index covering `org_id`, so the 1.2-1.6 s is a seq scan of 4.2M rows
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is an unbounded list appended on every request on every route ... replace timings with `collections.deque(maxlen=10000)`
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict; ... make the geo cache a `cachetools.TTLCache`
citations.F7: then verify: p95 for acme should drop to under 300 ms, `/healthz` should stay under 50 ms during a limit=1000 request
citations.F9: Do not ship the proposal: 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections (will hit max_connections and slow every route), and the Redis key includes `since`
citations.F11: the Redis key includes `since`, which defaults to `now()-30d` at microsecond precision, so the mobile client would never get a cache hit
